log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Down 0-1, must counter the rain core that beat me in G1. Lead Tyranitar+Excadrill: Sand Stream overrides Drizzle, Sand Rush Excadrill is my only speed answer to Swift Swim Swampert and Choice Scarf Basculegion — but Protect Excadrill early to preserve it. Back Gengar (Mega for Shadow Tag to trap/remove Basculegion or Primarina; Sludge Bomb OHKOs Primarina after chip) and Grimmsnarl (Prankster Taunt shuts potential Whimsicott Encore/Tailwind; Reflect/Light Screen mitigates Swampert EQ spread and Basculegion Wave Crash). Covers all opponent adjustments: same rain core, Whimsicott swap, or Forretress swap.
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent won G1 with rain core (Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion/Primarina). Leading Tyranitar+Excadrill for sand+Sand Rush speed control; back Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag trap) + Grimmsnarl (Taunt/screens). Plan: Protect Excadrill T1-2 to preserve Sand Rush answer for Swampert; Mega Evolve Gengar ASAP for Shadow Tag; use Grimmsnarl Taunt to deny Tailwind/Encore if Whimsicott appears. Thunder Wave useless on Swampert (Water/Ground immunity). If Forretress appears, Excadrill EQ handles it. Gengar-Mega base 130 Speed outspeeds most rain team except Swift Swim Swampert in rain.

decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper and Swampert to overwrite Tyranitar's sand with Drizzle and pressure with Mega Swampert under rain, bringing Basculegion and Primarina in the back to clean up.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 lead: Pelipper + Swampert vs Tyranitar + Excadrill. Back: Basculegion, Primarina. Game 1 won; keep applying rain pressure.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar Rock Slide chunks Pelipper for 40-77% (SE spread) while Tyranitar safely survives any combination of Swampert EQ (44-66%) + Pelipper Hurricane (8-13%). Excadrill Protects to preserve Focus Sash and full HP — at 280 Speed it outspeeds the entire rain core even through Tailwind or Swift Swim, making it the decisive threat for next turn. This follows the pre-game plan to shield Excadrill early and maintain sand dominance.
decisions.notebook: G2 T1: Sand active (5 turns), Excadrill 280 Spe outspeeds all rain mons even with Tailwind or Swift Swim in rain. Passho Berry on Tyranitar halves Liquidation to 26-38%. Swampert EQ does 44-66% to Tyranitar, 81-119% to Excadrill (Sash saves). Double Rock Slide would do 74-141% combined to Pelipper (potential KO). Plan: preserve Excadrill T1-2, chunk Pelipper with Rock Slide, bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag when safe, Grimmsnarl for Taunt/screens vs Whimsicott. Thunder Wave useless on Swampert (Ground immunity).

decisions.rationale: Setting Tailwind with Pelipper lets Swampert outspeed Excadrill under sand (or double rain/speed control) and safely mega evolve and strike Tyranitar with Liquidation.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T1: Pelipper Tailwind, Swampert Mega Liquidation onto Tyranitar.

decisions.rationale: Swampert-Mega (180-244 Spe with Tailwind) is guaranteed to KO Tyranitar (59% HP) with either Earthquake or Liquidation before Tyranitar can move (81 Spe). Tyranitar must Protect to survive. Excadrill (280 Spe) outspeeds everything; Rock Slide is SE on Pelipper (33.5-63.7%, potential KO from 38%) and hits Swampert NVE with a flinch chance. Excadrill's Focus Sash saves it from Swampert's Earthquake (81-119%). If Pelipper survives at low HP, Tyranitar Rock Slide guaranteed KOs it next turn (40.7-77% > remaining HP). This preserves Tyranitar for the Pelipper KO next turn while Excadrill chips both foes.
decisions.notebook: G2 T2: Swampert-Mega guaranteed KOs Tyranitar from 59% with EQ (59.5-83.1%) or Liquidation (67.7-95.4%) — Tyranitar must Protect when Swampert is active. Tyranitar Rock Slide guaranteed KOs Pelipper from ≤40.7% (does 40.7-77%). Excadrill Rock Slide does 33.5-63.7% to Pelipper — not a guaranteed KO from 38%. Plan T3: if Pelipper survived, Tyranitar Rock Slide KOs it; then consider switching to Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag to prevent opponent switches, or Grimmsnarl for screens/Taunt vs Whimsicott. Excadrill Sash likely broken if Swampert EQ'd T2 — switch out if at 1 HP. Sandstorm has 3 turns left after T2; may need Tyranitar to stay alive to refresh sand for Excadrill's Sand Rush.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, Pelipper outspeeds Excadrill and Tyranitar. Swampert-Mega Earthquake hits both Tyranitar and Excadrill super-effectively, picking up massive damage or KOs (both are weak to Ground). Pelipper uses Hurricane on Tyranitar (or Excadrill), ensuring heavy neutral or super-effective pressure while avoiding hitting our own Swampert with Weather Ball.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: T1 established Tailwind and chunked Tyranitar. T2 double target into the active slots with Hurricane + Earthquake clears or heavily damages Tyranitar and Excadrill.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper fainted last turn, so we bring in Basculegion to clean up. Excadrill is at 1% and Tyranitar protected last turn (so Protect success rate is reduced). Swampert-Mega passes or uses a move if needed, but since Slot 2 is locked to 'Pass' per the prompt menu for Swampert when replacing a fainted Pokémon, we select Pass for Swampert and Basculegion for the incoming slot.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: T1 Pelipper set Tailwind, Swampert Mega Evolved and hit Tyranitar. T2 Excadrill survived Earthquake at 1% due to Focus Sash. Bring in Basculegion to revenge kill.

decisions.rationale: Both active mons are in mortal danger. Tyranitar (59%) is guaranteed KO'd by Swampert-Mega; switching to Grimmsnarl preserves Tyranitar for later sand refresh and brings in a fresh Prankster user that survives any single hit from both foes (Wave Crash 64-95%, EQ 39-55%). Excadrill (1%) Protects — its Protect wasn't used last turn so success rate is normal. The opponent most likely targets Excadrill's slot (1% HP, obvious KO) which is blocked by Protect, meaning Grimmsnarl likely only takes one hit and survives comfortably. Next turn: Grimmsnarl uses Reflect (Prankster priority +4) while Excadrill switches to Gengar-Mega behind Reflect — Gengar-Mega then survives Wave Crash (~60-88%) and Liquidation (~41-57%) under Reflect, activating Shadow Tag to trap both opponent Pokemon. Gengar-Mega cannot switch in safely without Reflect (OHKO'd by nearly everything). Main risk: opponent predicts Protect and double-targets Grimmsnarl (~108% combined, potential KO), but this is less likely than the obvious play of targeting the 1% Excadrill.
decisions.notebook: G2 T3 plan: Tyranitar→Grimmsnarl switch, Excadrill Protect. T4 plan: Grimmsnarl Reflect (Prankster) + Excadrill→Gengar-Mega switch behind Reflect for Shadow Tag. Gengar-Mega damage benchmarks WITHOUT Reflect: Basculegion Wave Crash 120-175% (guaranteed OHKO), Swampert EQ 145-203% (guaranteed OHKO SE on Poison), Swampert Liquidation 82-115% (possible OHKO). WITH Reflect: Wave Crash ~60-88% (survives), Liquidation ~41-57% (survives), EQ ~72-101% (borderline). Grimmsnarl benchmarks: Wave Crash 64-95% (survives), EQ 39-55% (survives), Liquidation ~44% (survives), Aqua Jet 23-33% (survives). Double-target on Grimmsnarl: Wave Crash + Liquidation ≈ 108%+ (KO). Sandstorm 3 turns left (expires end of T5 unless Tyranitar returns). Opponent Tailwind 2 turns left (expires end of T4). After Tailwind expires: Excadrill 280 (Sand Rush) outspeeds Basculegion 147-195 (Scarf only); Gengar-Mega 165-200 outspeeds Swampert-Mega 90-122. Tyranitar preserved on bench at 59% — can refresh sand later. Opponent 4th mon unknown (Primarina/Whimsicott/Forretress, only one in this game).

decisions.rationale: Excadrill is at 1% and outspeeds Swampert under sand. Basculegion with Choice Scarf and Tailwind easily outspeeds and can finish off Excadrill with Wave Crash (or Aqua Jet, but Wave Crash into Excadrill guarantees the KO even if Excadrill somehow protected, though Excadrill used Protect last turn so it's vulnerable). Swampert can use Liquidation into Excadrill (or foe Tyranitar) or attack safely, but targeting Excadrill with Basculegion's Wave Crash guarantees removal of the Sand Rush threat, while Swampert uses Liquidation into Excadrill or Tyranitar. Wait, if Excadrill is at 1%, Wave Crash into Excadrill finishes it instantly. Let's make sure Swampert uses Liquidation on Excadrill or Tyranitar as well. Alternatively, Swampert can target Tyranitar while Basculegion takes out Excadrill. Let's check Slot 2 index 2: Liquidation -> foe 2 (Excadrill). Actually, Excadrill is at 1% HP, so either Basculegion's Wave Crash -> foe 2 (Excadrill) or Swampert's Liquidation -> foe 2 (Excadrill) will KO it. Let's have Basculegion use Wave Crash -> foe 2 (Excadrill) and Swampert use Liquidation -> foe 1 (Tyranitar).
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Pelipper fainted turn 2, Basculegion brought in safely. Excadrill is at 1% and Tyranitar at 59%.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill at 1% cannot survive any hit and is outsped by Scarf Basculegion under Tailwind. Switching to Gengar brings in the Gengarite holder for Mega Evolution + Shadow Tag, trapping both opponent Pokémon as Tailwind expires. Grimmsnarl Reflect via Prankster priority resolves before all opponent moves, halving physical damage to protect Gengar on entry. With Reflect, Gengar survives Wave Crash (~60-88%) and Liquidation (~41-57%); Earthquake is the borderline risk (~72-101%) but Swampert has favored Liquidation. Even in worst case, Grimmsnarl survives and Tyranitar remains on bench. Shadow Tag with Gengar-Mega outspeeding Swampert-Mega next turn (165-200 vs 90-122) is the win condition.
decisions.notebook: G2 T4 plan executed: Grimmsnarl Reflect (Prankster) + Excadrill→Gengar switch. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is the win con — after Tailwind expires T4, Gengar-Mega (165-200) outspeeds Swampert-Mega (90-122) and Basculegion (147-195 Scarf only). Sandstorm 2 turns left (expires end T5 unless Tyranitar returns). Tyranitar preserved at 59% for sand refresh. Opponent 4th mon unknown (Primarina/Whimsicott/Forretress, only one in game). G3 prep: opponent team is Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion + 1 unknown; consider leading Tyranitar+Excadrill again or Gengar+Grimmsnarl for early Shadow Tag. Key benchmark: Gengar-Mega WITH Reflect survives Wave Crash and Liquidation, borderline on Earthquake.

decisions.rationale: Send in Excadrill (1% HP, sash gone) as the sacrifice — Basculegion is Choice-locked into Wave Crash which guaranteed KOs Tyranitar from 59% even through Reflect, so sending Tyranitar in wastes our sand refresher. By sacrificing Excadrill, we preserve Tyranitar for sand refresh and keep a real combatant. Best case: opponent splits targets, leaving Grimmsnarl+Tyranitar vs 3 next turn. Worst case equals the worst case of sending Tyranitar. Grimmsnarl Passes (already used Reflect this turn). Do not forfeit — must win G2 to force G3.
decisions.notebook: G2 T4 end: Gengar fainted to Wave Crash, sending Excadrill as sacrifice. Tyranitar preserved at 59% for sand refresh — never send it into Basculegion Wave Crash (guaranteed KO even through Reflect). Opponent: Swampert-Mega 78% + Basculegion 64% (Scarf-locked Wave Crash) + 1 unknown (Primarina/Whimsicott/Forretress). Reflect up 8 turns. Sandstorm 2 turns left (expires end T5 unless Tyranitar enters). G3 prep: opponent rain team is Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion+1; Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag was the planned win con but Gengar died before mega-evolving. Consider leading Gengar+Grimmsnarl in G3 for early Shadow Tag, or Tyranitar+Excadrill for sand control. Key: Basculegion Adaptability Wave Crash is extremely dangerous — 120 BP STAB with Adaptability deals massive neutral damage even through Reflect.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill is at 1% HP, and Grimmsnarl just entered last turn (likely setting up Reflect/Light Screen). Basculegion is locked into Wave Crash, so hitting Excadrill with Wave Crash (or Swampert using Liquidation on Excadrill) easily finishes off the 1% Excadrill, while the other Pokémon targets Grimmsnarl or protects. Wait, Swampert cannot target slot 2 (Excadrill) with Liquidation if Excadrill is slot 2? Let's check: Excadrill is slot 2, Grimmsnarl is slot 1. Swampert Liquidation -> foe 2 (Excadrill) is choice 2. Basculegion Wave Crash -> foe 2 (Excadrill) is choice 1. However, if Excadrill uses Protect or switches/whatever, but Excadrill used Protect on turn 3 so its protect success rate is reduced or it might not protect. Even better, Basculegion's Wave Crash into Excadrill (choice 1) and Swampert's Liquidation into Grimmsnarl (choice 1 for Swampert) or Ice Punch into Grimmsnarl or Earthquake ensures damage. Let's make sure Excadrill faints: Basculegion Wave Crash into Excadrill (1) + Swampert Liquidation into Excadrill (2) guarantees removing the threat regardless of what Grimmsnarl does, or Swampert uses Liquidation into Excadrill and Basculegion hits Grimmsnarl. But since Basculegion is choice-locked into Wave Crash, Basculegion MUST use Wave Crash. Basculegion hitting Excadrill (choice 1) will KO Excadrill. Swampert can use Liquidation into Grimmsnarl (choice 1) or Ice Punch into Grimmsnarl (choice 4). Let's use Basculgion -> Wave Crash -> foe 2 (Excadrill) and Swampert -> Liquidation -> foe 1 (Grimmsnarl). Wait, if Grimmsnarl uses Reflect, hitting it with Liquidation is solid. Let's review Swampert options: 1 is Liquidation -> foe 1 (Grimmsnarl). Basculegion option 1 is Wave Crash -> foe 2 (Excadrill).

Excadrill at 1% will die this turn but outspeeds everything (280 Sand Rush) and gets Rock Slide off first — hits both foes with 30% flinch each, chipping Basculegion (16-31%) and Swampert (6-11%). Grimmsnarl Spirit Break on Basculegion (24-45%) stacks with Rock Slide for 40-76% combined, potentially KOing or leaving Basculegion in Tyranitar Crunch range next turn. Both foes will likely target the 1% Excadrill (SE guaranteed KO) keeping Grimmsnarl safe. Next turn Excadrill faints, Tyranitar enters to refresh sand. Must win G2 to force G3.
decisions.notebook: G2 T5: Excadrill sacrificed with Rock Slide + Grimmsnarl Spirit Break on Basculegion. Next turn bring Tyranitar to refresh sand. G3 plan: opponent rain team Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion+1. Basculegion Adaptability Wave Crash is the biggest threat — Thunder Wave from Tyranitar could cripple it. Consider leading Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl G3 for sand+screens, or Gengar+Grimmsnarl for Shadow Tag trap. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is win con if it survives to mega-evolve. Opponent likely brings Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion/Whimsicott or Primarina in G3.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Excadrill is at 1% HP under Sand (and Sandstorm ends this turn), but Basculegion outspeeds with Choice Scarf and can pick off Excadrill with Wave Crash. Swampert-Mega can use Liquidation into Excadrill (or Grimmsnarl) to guarantee the KO if priority/targeting needs redundancy, but target 2 (Excadrill) for Basculegion and target 2 (Excadrill) for Swampert is safe. Wait, Swampert Liquidation into Excadrill (choice 2) ensures Excadrill faints immediately before it can move, and Basculegion's Wave Crash into Excadrill (choice 1) also KOs. Let's check Swampert slot 2: Liquidation -> foe 2 (Excadrill).
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Tyranitar)
decisions.rationale: Opponent can KO Tyranitar (59%) with a double target: Liquidation does 45-64% through Reflect and Moonblast does 37-53%, totaling 82-117% — guaranteed KO. Tyranitar must Protect to survive. Grimmsnarl at 13% is dead to any hit (Moonblast guaranteed KO), so its only guaranteed-value play is Light Screen via Prankster priority, which goes up before any opponent move. Next turn Tyranitar faces the 1v2 with both Reflect and Light Screen active, letting it Thunder Wave and chip down Swampert (68%) and Primarina (100%) with neutralized SE hits.
decisions.notebook: G2 T6: Grimmsnarl Light Screen + Tyranitar Protect. Opponent can double-target Tyranitar for guaranteed KO (Liquidation 45-64% through Reflect + Moonblast 37-53% = 82-117%). Grimmsnarl is guaranteed dead to Moonblast. Plan: survive this turn with both screens up, then 1v2 grind with Thunder Wave speed control. G3 plan unchanged: opponent rain team Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion+1. Basculegion Adaptability Wave Crash biggest threat — Thunder Wave from Tyranitar to cripple. Consider leading Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl for sand+screens, or Gengar+Grimmsnarl for Shadow Tag trap. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is win con if it survives to mega-evolve.

decisions.rationale: Primarina's Hyper Voice (powered by Liquid Voice as a Water-type spread move) hits both Grimmsnarl (at 13% HP) and Tyranitar through Reflect, finishing off Grimmsnarl and dealing heavy damage to Tyranitar. Swampert-Mega's Earthquake hits both opponents for spread damage as well, synergizing to wipe out the remaining foes.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 ending; opponent brought Tyranitar, Excadrill, Grimmsnarl, and Gengar.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Tyranitar is my last Pokémon at 59% facing a guaranteed double-target KO (Liquidation 45-64% + Moonblast 25-35% = 70-99% > 59% HP). Swampert outspeeds and Primarina may too, so no attacking move can prevent the KO. Protect is the only option that can block both incoming hits; at ~33% consecutive-use success rate it's strictly better than Rock Slide (~20% survival needing Primarina to underspeed + low Liquidation roll + 90% accuracy) or Thunder Wave (~0% if double-targeted). If Protect works, Primarina dies to sandstorm (1% HP, not Rock/Ground/Steel immune), leaving a winnable 1v1: Tyranitar 59% vs Swampert 68% with screens still up and Thunder Wave available for speed control. Grimmsnarl is fainted — Pass.
decisions.notebook: G3 plan: opponent rain team Pelipper/Swampert-Mega/Basculegion+1 (likely Primarina or Whimsicott). Basculegion is Choice Scarf Adaptability Wave Crash — biggest offensive threat, Thunder Wave from Tyranitar cripples it (Water/Ghost not immune). Swampert-Mega Swift Swim outspeeds in rain; sand override from Tyranitar is critical to neutralize. Lead options: Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl for sand+screens+TWave, or Gengar+Grimmsnarl for Shadow Tag trap (Gengar-Mega must survive turn 1 to mega-evolve — risky into rain team's fast Water moves). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is primary win con if it can mega-evolve safely. Excadrill sand rush cleaner under sand. Key: get sand up to override Drizzle, use screens to survive Basculegion/Swampert hits, TWave speed control on non-Ground targets.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar used Protect on turn 6, so its Protect success rate is reduced, but it cannot use Protect successfully twice in a row anyway. Primarina has 1 HP and Tyranitar is at 59% with Reflect and Light Screen up, plus Sandstorm active. Moonblast deals heavy Fairy damage to Tyranitar (super-effective), and Swampert-Mega's Liquidation deals huge Water damage. Targeting Tyranitar with Moonblast and Liquidation guarantees a KO through screens.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 final turn closing out series 2-0.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2. In Game 2, the Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag plan backfired immediately: Basculegion's Adaptability Wave Crash OHKO'd Gengar on turn 4 before it could Mega Evolve, eliminating the planned win condition. The sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) traded poorly against rain Water spam—both are Water-weak and were overwhelmed by Swampert-Mega and Basculegion's raw power even with screens support. Tyranitar's consecutive Protect on turn 7 failed, leaving it exposed to a double-up KO. Hydrapple, which resists Water and was registered, was left on the bench—a critical bring error. The opponent's Tailwind from Pelipper provided speed control that sand override alone couldn't fully neutralize, and their rain team simply outpowered a roster with too many Water-weak picks.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Hydrapple over Gengar against this rain build—its Grass/Dragon typing resists Water and checks Swampert-Mega/Basculegion/Primarina far better. Drop the Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag plan entirely against rain; it cannot safely evolve through Adaptability Wave Crash or rain-boosted Water moves. Consider Vaporeon (Water Absorb) from the bench if available in future series for additional Water immunity. Prioritize Thunder Wave on Basculegion or Swampert early, and avoid consecutive Protect calls that risk failing under pressure.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs rain: Pelipper (DampRock Drizzle, Tailwind speed control, Weather Ball/Hurricane), Swampert-Mega (Adamant, Swift Swim, Earthquake/Liquidation/Ice Punch/Protect—primary physical wallbreaker), Basculegion (Choice Scarf Adaptability, Wave Crash/Last Respects/Aqua Jet/Flip Turn—extremely dangerous, OHKOs most non-resists through rain), Primarina (Modest, MysticWater, LiquidVoice Hyper Voice/Moonblast/Icy Wind/Protect—special cleaner), Whimsicott (FocusSash Prankster, Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect—speed control backup), Forretress (Sitrus Sturdy, BodyPress/GyroBall/StealthRock/Protect—defensive pivot). Opponent leads Pelipper+Swampert, uses Tailwind turn 1 for speed, then swaps Basculegion in to sweep with Wave Crash. Sand override from Tyranitar is necessary but insufficient alone—Tailwind still gives Swampert speed advantage. Key prep: Water-resist or Water-immune mons are mandatory; Hydrapple (Grass/Dragon) is the best registered answer. Gengar-Mega cannot safely evolve against this team. Thunder Wave is valuable but must land before Basculegion accumulates kills (Last Respects scaling). Opponent will protect Swampert and sack Pelipper early to maintain offensive pressure.

reflections.summary: You won the series 2-0 by effectively leveraging your rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion) alongside Primarina to break down the opponent's sand-and-screens structure. In Game 2, Pelipper's Tailwind setup and Swampert's heavy physical pressure overwhelmed Tyranitar and Excadrill early, while Basculegion cleaned up Gengar and Excadrill. Though screen support prolonged the game, Primarina and Mega Swampert systematically dismantled the remaining threats to close out the sweep.
reflections.adjustment: No further adjustments are needed since the series is won 2-0. For future matchups against similar sand-and-screen archetypes, continuing to lead weather control and high-offensive-pressure pivots like Pelipper and Mega Swampert remains a winning formula.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favored a sand core featuring Tyranitar (Passho Berry), Excadrill (Focus Sash), Gengar (Mega), and Grimmsnarl (Light Clay). Roster choices of Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Primarina effectively countered their speed control and defensive screens. Maintain proactive rain positioning and high-damage physical/special wallbreaking against Prankster screen setters.
